nodes.label: Synthetic Realism
nodes.description: The realistic representation of a different reality (cyborg/computer vision) rather than natural reality; conceptually pioneered by Georges Méliès.

nodes.label: Photorealism (Computer Graphics)
nodes.description: The ability of computer imagery to simulate the photographic lens (including its artifacts like depth of field, motion blur) rather than direct human perception.

nodes.label: Jurassic Park (Aesthetic)
nodes.description: The technique of artificially degrading perfect computer-generated graphics to match the grain and flaws of traditional film. Compared to Socialist Realism.

nodes.label: Socialist Realism
nodes.description: The superimposition of a perfect, idealized future onto the flawed, everyday present, analogous to Jurassic Park blending perfect CG with grainy film.

nodes.label: Meta-realism
nodes.description: A new realism based on the cyclical oscillation between an illusion and its suspension or destruction, typical of interactive media.

nodes.label: Phatic Function (Contact)
nodes.description: Communication dominated by the physical channel and act of connection, evident in web delays and loading sequences where the machine reveals itself.

nodes.label: Cognitive Multitasking
nodes.description: The rapid alternation between different kinds of attention and mental sets demanded by modern human-computer interfaces and interactive media.

nodes.label: Cinematic Realism
nodes.description: A historical standard of illusionism striving for a total approximation of reality (Bazin) or a substitution of codes (Comolli) driven by industrial aims (Bordwell & Staiger).

nodes.label: Image-Interface / Image-Instrument
nodes.description: Images transformed from passive representations into active tools that the user interacts with or uses to control reality.
